trials.notes: Passed 8/8. Correctly used WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment(), next_tag('H1'), depth-bounded next_token() traversal, #text filtering, and get_modifiable_text() for decoded text. The is_tag_closer() guard after plain next_tag('H1') is redundant because closers are skipped by default, but it is documented and harmless.

Passed 8/8. This is essentially the canonical documented subtree text walk: HTML Processor fragment parsing, first H1 opener, recorded current depth, next_token() while depth remains within the subtree, and decoded #text accumulation. No undocumented calls or misuse.

Passed 8/8. Correct processor choice and idiomatic token walking. Uses the documented break-on-depth-drop form, filters to ordinary #text tokens, and relies on get_modifiable_text() for decoded UTF-8 text. No undocumented calls or misuse.

failure_analysis: No hidden cases failed in any trial. The rendered docs did well on the decisive points: Tag Processor > Which processor should I use directs DOM-style text extraction to WP_HTML_Processor; HTML Processor > Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree gives almost the exact pattern of create_fragment(), next_tag(), get_current_depth(), next_token(), #text, and get_modifiable_text(); next_token() explains that walks do not stop automatically at the earlier matched element and must be depth- or breadcrumb-bounded; get_current_depth() explicitly calls out the >= boundary and virtual closers for malformed or unclosed input; get_modifiable_text() states that #text output is decoded and that the method is not itself a predicate for ordinary text. The only near-miss was trial-1 and trial-2 adding an unnecessary is_tag_closer() check after next_tag('H1'), even though next_tag() documents that closers are skipped by default. That did not affect behavior or API adherence.

doc_gaps.problem: The default tag_closers behavior is documented, but subjects still added redundant is_tag_closer() guards after plain next_tag('TAG').
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short example contrasting next_tag('DIV') with next_tag(array('tag_name'=>'DIV','tag_closers'=>'visit')), showing that is_tag_closer() is only needed in the latter case.

doc_gaps.problem: The Tag Processor page contains a lexical token-scanning text example after warning that DOM-style text extraction should use WP_HTML_Processor. This could still tempt readers to use the lower-level processor for subtree text tasks.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Make that snippet self-contained and label it as a flat whole-document lexical scan; add a one-line cross-reference to the HTML Processor subtree text recipe for element text content.

doc_gaps.problem: The decoded-text contract is clear, but the distinction between ordinary container text and opener-carried special-element text is spread across several paragraphs.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact return-contract table listing #text, ordinary element openers, comments, TITLE/TEXTAREA, and SCRIPT/STYLE, with decoded/raw/empty behavior for each token category.
